subject: Discovery recap: function calls, structured output, and contractual formatting
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finqueue.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: function calls, structured output, and contractual formatting

Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick written recap so we have a single reference for the engineering and procurement teams.

Top-level pain points you shared:
- Current agent orchestration is brittle when downstream consumers expect strict JSON. Outputs vary between model runs and require heavy post-processing.
- Latency spikes for structured outputs (the current median for schema responses is inconsistent when prompt traffic increases).
- Audit and schema compliance for finance flows is a blocker for procurement (they need deterministic formatting and verifiable provenance).

Current stack notes (what you told us):
- Backend: Python microservices with a LangChain-based orchestration layer + a small fleet of serverless functions for action execution.
- Client: Node service calling orchestration RPCs, ingesting structured JSON for downstream billing/clearing pipelines.
- Logging: S3 event logs + Mixpanel for usage metrics.

Success criteria you outlined:
- >99% schema validation pass rate for top-500 production prompts after integration (no silent field drift).
- Median end-to-end time for structured outputs < 200 ms under normal load.
- JSON outputs that are machine-parseable with explicit error codes for fallback logic.

What we propose as next steps (short, actionable):
1) Redwood supplies a minimal \"handshake\" JSON spec (fields, required types, example payloads) for the top-3 actions you called out. (See attached proposed-handshake-spec.json stub.)
2) Technical POC: sandbox with two Redwood endpoints mirroring your production traffic for 48 hours. We’ll run your top-500 prompts and report schema pass/fail, latency percentiles, and mismatches.
3) Contractual formatting appendix: we’ll provide a short appendix you can attach to an SOW that defines deterministic formatting acceptance criteria.
4) Follow-up call: propose Wed 2026-10-13 at 10:00 AM PT (30 min) to review handshake and POC plan.

Attachments included: proposed-handshake-spec.json (application/json, 3 KB), redwood-dataflow.pdf (diagram, 120 KB).

If that summary matches your expectations, I’ll loop Neha (solutions lead) and Karthik (platform) to draft the handshake and POC details.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

This is spot on. A few clarifications from our side:
- Our production prompts are very templated; we can provide a representative set of ~600 queries (I called out 500 as a round number).
- Determinism means two things for us: schema validity (no missing/extra required fields) and a stable semantic mapping so our action executor receives consistent types and enums. We can tolerate field ordering variance as long as parsers can canonicalize, but enums must be exact.
- The orchestration layer you saw is a thin shim that maps agent outputs to function calls. The heavy lifting (auth, retries) is in our serverless functions.

Acceptance and procurement notes:
- Procurement wants the formatting appendix to include: schema versioning terms, rollback plan if a schema regression is detected, and a remediation SLA for critical regressions.
- Security review will require an S3 ingestion diagram (redwood-dataflow.pdf helped). We’ll share our internal orchestration doc (attached) so you have the exact RPC surface.

I’m good with the proposed POC. Wed 10/13 10:00 AM PT works. Please loop Neha.

Thanks,
Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finqueue.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Technical checklist: function calls, agent routing, and deterministic formatting

Alex / team — quick tech note ahead of the 10/13 call so we can be aligned on the POC engineering checklist. Short bullets:

- Function-call mapping: we will expose a JSON \"handshake\" that lists action names, required fields, and sample success/failure codes. The POC will accept calls to two sandbox actions (execute_payment, lookup_customer).
- Schema validation: Redwood will run an automated validator against each model output. Acceptance requires schema validation pass (jsonschema) and optional semantic checks (enum membership). We recommend tagging schemas with a version (e.g., v1.0) and including a schema_version field in every response to support rollbacks.
- Deterministic formatting criteria (proposed):
  * Required fields must always be present for success responses.
  * Enums and small vocab fields must match exactly (case-sensitive).
  * Ordering is not relied on by the parser — canonicalization is acceptable, but the POC should highlight outliers where field sets differ.
  * Any fallback (e.g., free-text in a "notes" field) must be accompanied by a structured "fallback_reason" code.
- Agent routing and fallbacks: Redwood supports routing by policy. For the POC we will send primary requests to the primary model and, on failure, fallback to a compatible variant with a degraded SLA. All fallbacks will be logged and surfaced in the validation report.
- Observability hooks: we’ll add a trace_id in the handshake so you can link events back to your serverless functions and S3 logs.

Attachments: agent-routing-matrix.csv (CSV, 2 KB) — contains an initial mapping of action -> model variant -> fallback policy.

I’ll prepare the minimal schema samples before our call and post them to the Drive link Marissa created. Looking forward to the POC.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Platform Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
